spans.quotation: Since APA does not direct or control the end use of our produced oil and gas, we exclude the calculation of Scope 3 emissions, which are dominated by category 11: use of sold products.

305-3 Other indirect (Scope 3) GHG emissions — Omitted: 305-3 — Reason: Information unavailable/incomplete — Explanation: Because there is currently no international guideline for the determination of energy consumption in Scope 3, we do not currently disclose the information required.

note: criteria — 0 of 5. Full exhaustive search conducted across all report sections: primary GHG text (pp. 38–39), Key Performance Data table (p. 128), TCFD Analysis appendix (pp. 134–141), GRI Content Index (pp. 148–153), IPIECA-API-IOGP index (pp. 154–156), and SASB Oil & Gas E&P index (pp. 156–157). No Scope 3 figure, category estimate, or methodology disclosure of any kind appears anywhere in the report. APA makes a deliberate policy exclusion with two separate rationales: (1) operational — it does not direct or control end use of produced oil and gas (p. 38), and (2) standards — it cites the absence of an international guideline for energy consumption in Scope 3 (GRI 305-3 omission, p. 151). The SASB index contains no EM-EP row for Scope 3. The TCFD section (pp. 134–141) explicitly states APA is 'focused on reducing Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions.' Category 11 (use of sold products) is acknowledged by name on p. 38 as the dominant category but is not quantified. Presence = NOT_DISCLOSED: no criterion is satisfied; this is an intentional exclusion, not a search gap. Confidence = High — exclusion is stated directly and confirmed across three independent sections of the report. Cross-concept note: the Scope 3 exclusion language on p. 38 is embedded within the M1 methodology span and is captured here for M3 documentation per handbook boundary guidance.
